title: Kubernetes
text: Kubernetes is an open-source container orchestration platform used to automate deployment, scaling and management of containerized applications. Kubernetes uses clusters, nodes, pods, deployments, services, ConfigMaps and Secrets to operate cloud-native workloads.

title: Docker
text: Docker packages applications and their dependencies into lightweight containers. Containers provide consistent environments across development, testing and production and are commonly used with CI/CD and Kubernetes.

title: AWS Cloud
text: Amazon Web Services provides cloud infrastructure and managed services including EC2, S3, IAM, VPC, Lambda, RDS and CloudWatch. AWS enables scalable and highly available cloud architectures.

title: DevOps
text: DevOps combines development and operations practices to automate software delivery. CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, containers, monitoring and automated testing are important DevOps practices.

title: Cloud Architecture
text: Cloud architecture combines compute, networking, storage, databases, security, observability and automation. Good cloud architecture focuses on reliability, scalability, security, performance and cost optimization.

title: CI/CD
text: Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery automate building, testing and deploying software. GitHub Actions and other CI/CD systems can automatically validate code and deploy applications after changes are pushed.

title: Terraform
text: Terraform is an infrastructure as code tool that allows engineers to define cloud and infrastructure resources using configuration files. Terraform supports repeatable infrastructure provisioning and automation.

title: Cloud Security
text: Cloud security protects infrastructure, applications, identities and data. Important practices include least privilege IAM, encryption, network segmentation, secrets management, logging, monitoring and continuous security validation.
